question: The following statements regarding insulin resistance in diabetic patients are true except:

options.opa: It is more common with huminsulin
options.opb: It may occur in the presence of infections
options.opc: It may be due to antibodies to insulin
options.opd: Use of glucocorticoids may be useful in severe cases

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Huminsulin" -> "synthetic human insulin" -> "similar resistance profile to other insulin types" -> "unlikely to be more common with huminsulin" -> 20%
CHAIN: "Infections" -> "stress response in body" -> "increased counter-regulatory hormones" -> "increased insulin resistance" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Antibodies to insulin" -> "immune response against insulin" -> "reduced insulin efficacy" -> "increased insulin resistance" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Glucocorticoids" -> "increase in blood glucose levels" -> "worsen insulin resistance" -> "not useful in severe cases of insulin resistance" -> 15%
analysis: After evaluating each option against standard medical knowledge, it is clear that glucocorticoids, mentioned in option opd, would not be beneficial for managing insulin resistance. This is because they typically raise blood glucose levels and impair insulin action, contrary to what would be desired in managing insulin resistance. The other options are consistent with known medical facts about insulin resistance.
